column1: # One row per rule.  A rule is either a directory prefix ("corpus/learn/") or
# longest matching rule governs a path, so a file rule overrides its tree and a
# deeper directory overrides a shallower one.  Every tracked path and every
# corpus page must resolve to exactly one rule -- tools/check-licenses.py
# redistribution: yes | no | unclear  -- may the bytes be published as they are?
#   yes     a statement grants redistribution with conditions (the conditions
#   no      a statement forbids it, or states all rights reserved, or no
#   unclear no statement of its own: the pages it derives from govern it, or
#           the project has published no licence at all
# evidence is a file in this repository, quote is the wording read from it
# (verbatim, whitespace aside).  "-" means no statement was located for the
# item; that is a finding, not a gap to be filled by guessing.

column4: Five commercially published Microsoft Press books (Programmer's Guide 1998 and 1999, Communications Guide 1999, User Interface Services Guide 1999, Device Driver Kit 1999), scanned, mirrored on bitsavers.trailing-edge.com and kept verbatim here. Each copyright page reads 'PUBLISHED BY Microsoft Press' and reserves all rights with an express prohibition on reproducing or transmitting any part of the contents without the publisher's written permission; each carries an ISBN and a Library of Congress CIP record. These are retail books, not free product documentation, and queues/third-party-sources.md records the opposite decision for the same bitsavers directory ('these stay uncollected'). 117 MB of them are tracked by git in a public repository.
column6: No part of the contents of this book may be reproduced or transmitted in any form or by any means without the written permission of the publisher.

column4: A third-party commercial book: 'Windows CE 3.0: Application Programming', Prentice Hall PTR, 2001, ISBN 0-13-025592-0, retail $49.99 U.S. / $75.00 Canada. Its copyright page reserves all rights and requires the publisher's written permission for any reproduction. The bundled CD-ROM described in the book carries Microsoft eMbedded Visual C++/Visual Basic 3.0 'reproduced by Prentice Hall PTR under a special arrangement with Microsoft Corporation', so two rightsholders restrict this one item. It is not Microsoft documentation and it is not an open-source artefact.
column6: No part of this book may be reproduced, in any form or by any means, without permission in writing from the publisher.
